elements.quote: Among the studies included in this SRMA, six studies were in Amhara, four in SNNP region, two in Oromia, two in Addis Ababa, two in Harari, one in Dire Dawa and two in Tigray. Fourteen of the studies were cross sectional, four were cohort and one case control studies. A total of 8755 participants with the smallest 166 to the largest 1069 participants included and found the prevalence which ranges from 6.80 to 25.4% of SSI following cesarean section in Ethiopia. On the other hand, the quality of each study was assessed by using NOS, the score of all included studies lies between 8 to 9 which indicates good quality
elements.reason: Text briefly summarizes study characteristics (region, design, sample size) and risk of bias (NOS scores indicating good quality) for contributing studies.

elements.quote: The pooled estimate of SSI in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95%CI, 9.29-12.97%). Prolonged labor (AOR = 3.16, 95% CI; (2.14-4.68)), chorioamnionitis (AOR = 4.26, 95% CI; (1.99-8.91)), prolonged PROM (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.51-5.62)), repeated vaginal examination (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.45-5.88)), decreased hemoglobin level (AOR = 4.57, 95%CI; (3.16-6.60)), vertical skin incision (AOR = 3.09, 95% CI; (2.04-4.67)) and general anesthesia (AOR = 1.82, 95% CI (1.21-2.75)) are significantly associated with SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: Results of all statistical syntheses, including pooled prevalence and meta-analysis of predictors, are reported.

elements.quote: The pooled estimate of SSI in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95%CI, 9.29-12.97%). elements.reason: Summary estimates and precision (95% CIs) are reported for all meta-analyses (prevalence and predictors).
